segments: The 50th Jubilee.
Arab Kings.
That Nur al-Din died in Damascus of quinsy.
One of the skilled physicians of Damascus, known as al-Rahbi,
whom I, the weak one, reached two of his elderly sons, excellent physicians, recounted:
"After the illness grew severe upon him,
I was summoned, along with the rest of the physicians.
And when we entered,
we found him reclining in a very narrow, small room.
And we said
that a vein should be opened,
but he did not agree.
And because he was feared by everyone,
we were not able to press the matter upon him;
and at that very time he died."
For he was of a swarthy complexion,
tall of stature,
beardless
except for a few hairs beneath his chin,
simple in his manner and his dress,
and a great enemy of the Shiites who trace their lineage from Ali.
And he took more than fifty cities and fortresses from the Franks.
And he built a great hospital and a college in Damascus,
and the Great Mosque in Mosul.
And when Nur al-Din died,
Malik al-Salih Ismail, his son, stood up after him.
And all the grandees swore allegiance to him.
And Saladin also proclaimed him in Egypt,
and inscribed his name on the silver coins and the dinars.
And Sayf al-Din Ghazi, the lord of Mosul,
when {OCR?} he heard that his uncle Nur al-Din had died,
there was great rejoicing with him.
And heralds proclaimed in Mosul
that everyone openly drink, get drunk, and make merry.
And he gathered armies and came to Mesopotamia,
and took control of Edessa, Harran, and the rest of the places.
And the emir Shams al-Din, the commander-in-chief of Aleppo,
sent to the grandees in Damascus, saying:
"Bring Malik al-Salih to Aleppo,
otherwise it will slip from his hands."
The grandees, however, lest Shams al-Din gain control over the administration of the kingdom,
would not permit al-Salih to leave them.
And Saladin sent a censure to the grandees of Damascus:
"How did they neglect that the regions were being seized,
and did not inform him and call him to come help?" And he said to them further:
"If Nur al-Din had known that there was someone among you more watchful than I,
he would have entrusted to him the kingdom of Egypt.
And now, behold, I am arriving,
because the conduct of my lord and the son of my lord is fitting for me,
and not for you."
The grandees, then, sent al-Salih to Aleppo,
and he became his governor
